prompt: Propose a lot-level composite key and explain why the current asset-level duplicate rule would be wrong for it.
answer: For multiple positions propose a stable composite key(account_id,instrument_id,lot_id) within an explicitly identified valuation snapshot;include snapshot date/time and currency/context if several snapshots are processed together. Stable lot identifiers must come from the source or a documented mapping,not local row order. Two legitimate lots of one asset can coexist,so the current asset-only duplicate rule would wrongly quarantine them. Define duplicate/revision policy at the actual grain,validate quantity/price/multiplier conventions,and aggregate to asset only under an explicit model. No lot-aware cleaner was implemented.

prompt: Explain why relabeling EUR as USD without conversion is not cleaning.
answer: The original EURO record remains rejected as unsupported_currency with raw EUR retained. Uppercasing eur toEUR changes spelling only;rewriting EUR toUSD without an actual exchange-rate calculation would falsely change the unit label while leaving the numeric amount unchanged. FX valuation needs rate direction,valuation/availability time,source and precision policies,not a cleaning shortcut.

prompt: Design an expected-asset-set check that runs after rejection handling and before valuation.
answer: After resolving or explicitly handling every rejected key,compare the full intended accepted asset set with independently supplied expected_assets before publishing a batch valuation. Keep rejected expected assets visible as unresolved;do not derive the expected set from accepted rows or call an accepted subset complete. Reject/withhold missing,extra or unresolved keys;do not silently fill values,choose duplicate winners or relabel currencies. Planned cases:exact complete set accepts,missing record blocks,extra accepted asset blocks,expected key only in rejection blocks,duplicates remain unresolved,source-order change preserves set result. Current fixture has rejections and stays not ready. No expected-set gate or new acceptance tests were implemented.

prompt: Extend the audit with a source batch hash and policy version; distinguish those fields from the local row ordinal.
answer: The extension hashes a precisely declared canonical UTF8 JSON serialization of raw parsed records in source order,using fixed field order,compact separators,ensure_ascii=False and one final newline. source-batch.json retains those exact bytes. Decision/field-change rows carry source_batch_sha256 and policy_version=book1-7.8-strip-uppercase-currency-v1;source_hash_kind names this parsed-record serialization. Original pandas index labels are excluded deliberately;local ordinal resets per input and is not global identity. Same source records/order repeat the digest;reordering changes it. This is not the hash of an original CSV or vendor authentication. Retain original-file byte evidence separately when available and preserve the mapping to parsed records. A human policy-version label must be maintained when semantics change;it does not automatically attest implementation identity.
